title: Integer parameter compared with a number stored as text
prompt: Migration lookup, about 60 calls per second. Each call takes about 210 ms of CPU and about 4,400 logical reads and
returns 0 or 1 rows. Plan: Index Scan of IX_Customers_LegacyRef (2.0M rows) with predicate
CONVERT_IMPLICIT(int, c.LegacyRef, 0) = @LegacyRef and a PlanAffectingConvert warning. LegacyRef is varchar(9); the
application binds @LegacyRef as int, and that binding cannot change in this release: only the statement text can.
CK_Customers_LegacyRef allows digits only, with a first digit of 1 to 9.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

correct_families.description: Convert the parameter to text, wide enough for any int, so the column is compared in its own type and the index can seek.

traps.why: An explicit conversion of the column is the same scan as the implicit one.
An int converted to a varchar that is too short becomes '*'. A nine-digit reference then matches nothing.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case nine_digits: the baseline returns the customer, the rewrite returns no row.

traps.why: STR pads the number with leading spaces, so the text never equals a stored reference.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case existing_ref: the baseline returns the customer, the rewrite returns no row.

min_improvement.basis: The scan reads about 4,400 pages per call. A seek and one lookup read about 5.

key.reference_notes: The comparison as numbers and the comparison as text agree only because CK_Customers_LegacyRef forbids signs, spaces, leading zeros and the empty string. Without the constraint, '007' would match 7 in the baseline only.
